newsitem.title: USA: Harrah's to focus on new Tunica casino.
newsitem.headline: Harrah's to focus on new Tunica casino.

text.p: Harrah's, which reported a fourth quarter loss after charges, said on Thursday it will dedicate all of its efforts in Tunica, Miss., to its new Tunica Mardi Gras casino and it will have a plan on how to exit its old casino there by the middle of 1997.
Harrah's Tunica operations, as well as those in Vicksburg, Miss., broke even in 1996, the company said. Harrah's opened the Mardi Gras casino in April 1996, it said.

"1996 was a difficult year. Capacity additions in several markets across the country tipped the supply and demand balance," chairman, president and chief executive officer Philip Satre said in a statement.

For 1997, Harrah's aims to complete a new hotel tower and renovations at its Las Vegas casino. But disruptions from the constructuion are expected to continue during the first and second quarters, the company said.
Harrah's said it is opening a new hotel tower for its casino in Atlantic City, N.J., this summer.

Pending regulatory approval, Harrah's is scheduled to open a new casino at the end of the first quarter in St. Louis, it said. Also, its Harrah's Cherokee Smoky Mountains casino is set for a fall 1007 opening, the company said.
Harrah's said it received approval in late January for Harrah's Prairie Bank - Topeka, which is expected to open in late 1997.
